question.prompt: For \(f(x)=x^2\), \(x\in[-1,2]\), what is the minimum value?

solutions.explanation: The vertex at \(x=0\) lies in the interval \([-1,2]\), and \(f(0)=0\); the endpoint values are 1 and 4. The minimum value is 0.
solutions.title: Locate the vertex in the interval

solutions.explanation: Every real square is nonnegative, so \(f(x)=x^2\ge0\). Since \(0\in[-1,2]\) and \(f(0)=0\), this lower bound is attained. The minimum value is \(0\).
solutions.title: Use the sign of a square
